Mike starts his shift and encounters a violet figure at a locked door.
The terminal reports an access failure. A pair of blue lights waits beyond the door.
Mike sorts the tickets, maps the patterns and flags an anomalous transfer.
Felicia brings a violin into Mike’s investigation of the signal.
The day keeps moving while an automated recovery reports success.
Felicia plays as Mike compares the violin’s frequencies with the signal.
Mike and Felicia compare bearings against the waveform.
The invitation leads Mike and Felicia into the hangar.
Felicia plays beside the aircraft in the Morningstar hangar.
Mike and Felicia piece together the origin of Orpheus.
A test of the isolation circuit brings an unsolicited reply.
Mike stops the test and the team investigates the repeated route.
The team cuts the Morningstar route while the night crew waits on the apron.
Two prisoners meet across the fence in the orbital detention yard.
The masked prisoner and K talk about what they remember.
Oz and K exchange names through the vents between their cells.
The dogs find a route through the detention block.
K follows the dogs to the cell doors and the red-lit control.
The door to cell 1984 releases and Oz steps out.
Oz, K and the dogs reach an open door together.
At the shutter, Waldo wedges a cart under the door while K pulls the manual release. They run for the docking collar with the dogs.
The group crosses the docking collar toward the shuttle.
K and Oz speak aboard the shuttle with the dogs between them.
Under the stars, guitar and radio break the silence.
Six months later the shuttle approaches Earth.
A controller clears the shuttle. Waldo texts Mike that he is out of prison and invites him to the house. Mike replies that he is on his way.
Waldo welcomes Mike home with his wrestling mask set aside. He introduces K. Mike and K recognize each other’s voices and shake hands.
K and Mike discuss a sense of recognition as they help Felicia lift an instrument case in Waldo’s garage.
Oz and Felicia listen as Mike and K compare names and memories.
K and Mike listen at Waldo’s bench. Two panels from K’s memory show Iona in the Low Quarter.
Iona plays drums beside Red on guitar at a Ghost Bends show.
K recalls handing Iona the keys and the moment she left.
At Waldo’s house, K compares the capsule beacon with Mike’s badge alert and the later prison intake. Felicia listens as the cassette stops. K plays the final beat himself.
At K’s request, Mike pauses the prison relay that sent him fragments of Mike’s memories. K still remembers Mike’s street. Waldo recalls growing up there.
At Waldo’s house, K holds the embroidered patch bearing his chosen name. Waldo notices a loose stitch.
Felicia recognizes the prison relay’s chirp from her recording. They isolate the local box and carry it into Waldo’s house.
At their home workbench the crew hears the isolated prison unit answer. Dee and Priya join by video from AeroTech, where the same code can restart a test rig.
Dee, Priya and Mike weigh three ways of handling a test-rig fault. Dee asks who will answer the alarm at two in the morning.
Dee and Priya arrange coverage. At Waldo’s house the group records a two-person restart rule and K’s right to decide about his own feed.
K unplugs the memory feed and puts his cassette in a drawer. At AeroTech, staff check and sign before restarting the rig.
The first morning brings a ticket for human review.
Mike returns to the maintenance queue and checks the first label.
An aligned shipping label comes out of the printer. On the back Marcus has drawn the guide that kept slipping.
Volume Two cover. The Vessel pairs K in custody with Iona on the roadside.
Officers enter the Ghost Bends performance and confront Red.
Red gives Iona his car keys and tells her to go.
Iona blinds the camera, races past the fence and climbs into the coupe.
Iona evades pursuit, jumps the broken dock and lands. Facing the road, she grips the wheel with both hands.
Iona drives toward daylight listening to Somewhere Deep Down Below.
Before the arrest, Red and Iona trace an observation route on a map.
After the arrest Red is taken aboard. Iona tries the radio.
Iona stops the car by the water as morning breaks.
Aboard the transport, Red works himself free of the restraints.
Red makes his way through the transport to the control room.
Red cuts the anchor and the control display reports the route lost.
Orbital custody processes Red at intake.
The detainee’s skills are retained while his memory is conditioned.
Alone in the cell, K tries the door controls.
In a Low Quarter recollection, Red and Iona share work across the bench.
Iona counts the band in and Ghost Bends takes the stage.
After the performance, Iona and Red discover their signal carried farther than intended.
Iona keeps a set list while Red heads toward the relay vault.
Red opens the way through the vault as the machinery fails.
Red and Iona confront the cost of the door he opened.
The Low Quarter begins calling Red El Mago Rojo.
Iona asks Red what he wants and hands him a guitar.
Red works at the bench and remembers the choice that brought him there.
The account of two realms reconciles seven Earth years with Red’s twenty-four.
The crossing record exposes what Orpheus wanted from Red.
K retrieves his belongings and attempts another escape.
The escape brings K back to the bunk in cell 118.
K listens to the hum behind the cell vent.
Life in the Low Quarter continues at the workbench and on the Ghost Bends stage.
The walls of cell 118 open onto an unfamiliar, luminous landscape.
K shares tea with Buddha and recognizes something familiar.
The robe recalls the name the vault workers gave their rescuer, El Mago Rojo. The teacher lets Red choose when to take off the ivory mask.
During the ascent, K lifts away the ivory mask. Under the green-and-gold hood his dark eyes show through square glasses. He says “El.”
Back in Cell 118, K listens at the vent. He keeps the face he saw beneath the mask, even as the words of the encounter slip away.
Volume Three cover. The Return Signal shows K in the workshop and Iona at the radio.
At Waldo’s home workshop, K plays guitar, opens the case and sets up the receiver.
Recovered custody records give Mike and K part of the crossing route.
K questions Orpheus about the missing years.
K names the interference and ends the connection.
A recording from the crossing survives in the Low Quarter.
Iona and her mentor recover a coil near the ruined crossing.
At the workshop they begin assembling the receiver.
On Earth, K calls Iona over the newly tuned set.
In the Low Quarter, Iona cuts transmission as the output stage overheats. The connection drops.
At Waldo’s garage, K and Mike trace the prison controller’s request to a data lead. They unplug it and keep the separate speaker line connected.
Mike and K rewire the set so the energy ends at the speaker.
During a storm Iona climbs to hold the receiver mast.
Iona and her mentor discuss what the connection will cost.
At Waldo’s house, Mike and K carry the repaired equipment outside for the roof antenna.
On the roof, K’s eyes widen when a falling bracket hangs in the air. His face tightens when it drops, then eases as Mike reaches up with the wrench.
On the narrower channel an unexplained late pulse appears.
Iona hears Red’s voice through the speaker.
K and Iona speak across the Earth and Low Quarter receivers.
Iona tells K she is angry and glad he survived.
At both ends of the connection they set limits and choose when to cut the call.
Life at both workbenches continues while the line waits.
End credits for Volume Three, The Return Signal.
Volume Four cover. The False Bearing pairs Iona’s field notes with a Ghost Bends performance.
Iona follows an increasingly strong reading toward an abandoned site.
K keys and releases his microphone. The pulses keep coming.
Iona’s mentor identifies an old beacon on the map.
Iona and her mentor mark the false bearing on the map.
Iona admits she followed the wrong signal while K stayed by the receiver.
Iona taps the snare and asks K if he remembers their count-in.
K agrees to meet tomorrow and picks up his guitar.
Iona closes her link log and returns to the drums. She leaves space on the fourth beat for her bandmates to come in.
End credits for Volume Four, The False Bearing.
